title: Correctness of sequential bit search
statement: Let $n,m$ be natural numbers, let $R$ be a relation between Boolean lists, and let $(D_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ be a family of Boolean circuits, with $D_j$ taking $n+j$ input bits. Suppose that for every $1\le j\le m$, every Boolean list $y$ of length $n$, and every Boolean list $p$ of length $j$, the circuit $D_j$ outputs true on the concatenation of $y$ and $p$ exactly when some extension of $p$ to a list of length $m$ is related to $y$ by $R$. If $y$ has length $n$ and some list of length $m$ is related to $y$ by $R$, then the list produced by the sequential search using these circuits is related to $y$ by $R$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $j$ with $1\le j\le m$, the stated circuit test is equivalent to existence of an $R$-related length-$m$ extension
